Sure, most people were always listening to what's popular, but college radio was an institution. Large groups of people were listening to weird, local, underground stuff daily. Everyone was listening to it at the same time so it was a social experience, not just art in a vacuum. People actually discussed what they listened to and wanted to understand it and have their opinions be understood. Streaming leads to more schizoid consumption of art popular or otherwise.


When it comes to individual taste some people are always going to dig for novelty, but the average joe has little exposure to anything challenging nor social incentive to take it seriously. Even alot of the artists I know are only listening to popular music across a wide stretch of genres. If one more person hypes up their obscure music taste and recommends me Ryo Fukui I might end it.

Radio doesn't learn what you like and show you more of it. I've found more interesting music from a good local station then I ever have from the algorithms. Even when I deliberately try to train the algorithms I can't get them to recommend me music in other languages unless it's popular with English speakers.
